July 1936: a military coup in Spain failed to take the whole country in days, like it was supposed to. Instead it triggered a war that split Spain in two for three years.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ July 1936: generals led by Franco rose against the Republic. The coup succeeded fast in the conservative north and northwest, but stalled at Madrid and Barcelona — leaving Spain roughly split between Nationalist and Republican zones within days.

2/ March 1937: Nationalist forces held most of the northwest and had pushed a wedge through the west-centre, while Republicans still controlled Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, most of the Mediterranean coast, and an isolated northern strip around Bilbao and Asturias.

3/ March-April 1938: the Aragon Offensive tore the Republic apart. On 15 April, Nationalist troops reached the Mediterranean at Vinaroz, cutting Republican territory in two — Catalonia sealed off in the northeast, Madrid and the south left to fight on alone.

4/ February 1939: Barcelona had fallen on 26 January and the rest of Catalonia followed within days. The Republic was down to a shrinking pocket around Madrid and Valencia. Franco declared final victory on 1 April 1939.
5/ Roughly half a million people died from combat, executions and disease over those 33 months. Franco then ruled Spain for the next 36 years, until his death in 1975.
